Job Description

The Clinical Program Coordinator (Infection Control) is responsible for the complex, multi-factorial, multi-disciplinary care coordination and independent management in Infection Control, which includes developing, evaluating and revising care pathways based on assessments conducted through engagement with the patient, family and multiple departments and disciplines. The Clinical Program Coordinator interfaces directly with MSH Departments, Administrators, Nursing, Medical and Quality leadership, and clinical staff and coordinates care for a patient population regarding the clinical, educational and operational impact of all care delivery, and outcome measures.

The Clinical Program Coordinator is responsible for program development, which includes the independent management of a program of care for a group of patients; carried out for the duration of hospitalization and includes changing practice to meet outcomes; evaluation of practice; providing just in time education and implementing corrective action plans. The Clinical Program Coordinator is expected to flex their work schedule to manage the above.

May be accountable for the collaborative development and execution of programmatic policies, procedures and guidelines, organization-wide.

This position reports directly to discipline leadership with a professional line to MSH Nursing or related disciplines professional practice leadership.

Qualifications

Using independent decision-making, the Clinical Program Coordinator establishes and implements short and long term goals, objectives, policies and operating procedures to ensure a high level of performance in nursing care delivery to the specialty patient population.

Education, Experience And Certifications

new_jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, WW Benchmarking and Scorecard (GSCE)
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon's Global Standards & Customer Excellence (GSCE) organization owns the Worldwide Scorecard - the mechanism that provides a holistic view of operational performance across Safety, People, Customer Experience, Quality, Cost, and Sustainability pillars for 1,000+ last-mile delivery stations and sort centers spanning North America, Europe, Japan, India, and ECCF. The WW Benchmarking team within GSCE manages performance benchmarking using the Continuous Benchmarking Rate Setting (CBRS) methodology - clustering stations into peer groups and setting statistically rigorous performance targets that control for non-ops factors.

As the Senior Program Manager for the Quality Pillar, you will own end-to-end benchmarking and scorecard strategy for First Pass Yield (FPY), Stow Buffer Compliance, and emerging quality metrics across all regions. You will drive the CBRS methodology for quality KPIs, launch and scale benchmarking studies that close performance gaps at underperforming stations, develop next-generation metrics that replace legacy measurements, and feed input-level KPIs into the Risk Engine that powers predictive operational alerts. You will partner with Operations, ACES, BIE (Analytics), and Finance teams to ensure quality benchmarks are accurate, equitable, and drive measurable operational improvement across stations worldwide.

This role requires strong analytical thinking, program management rigor, and the ability to translate complex statistical methodologies into operator-friendly insights. You will manage multiple concurrent workstreams - from quarterly benchmark refreshes, to multi-month benchmarking studies with site-level interventions, to expanding quality benchmarks to new regions and business units where none previously existed. You will also build AI-powered tooling that accelerates validation and delivery, and contribute input signals to the Gravion Risk Engine. Cross-team coordination, data fluency, stakeholder communication to senior leadership, and a bias for automation are essential.

You will be a strong partner of Central and Field ACES teams - delivering operator sentiment of the metrics, benchmarking the metrics and aligning closely with their OP process, initiating metric changes, and maintaining metric parity around the world.

Key job responsibilities

Own the Quality Pillar benchmarking portfolio end-to-end — vision, methodology, and cadence for FPY, Stow Buffer Compliance, and future quality metrics across NA, EU, JP, ECCF, RSR, and RoW
Drive benchmarking methodology for quality KPIs — quarterly benchmark generation, cluster design, sub-cluster coefficients, and statistical model improvement
Design benchmarking studies identifying root causes at underperforming stations, sharing best practices, and driving measurable quality improvement
Expand quality benchmarks to new regions and BUs — adapting methodology for local data, gaining alignment, and launching benchmarks where none existed
Own Road to CBRS (benchmarking) for quality metrics — translating benchmarks into actionable station-level insights that close the gap
Partner with Central and Field ACES on operator sentiment, OP alignment, and worldwide metric parity
Define upstream quality KPI signals for the Risk Engine — early-warning indicators and data integration partnership
Build AI-powered validation tooling — cluster analyzers, anomaly detection, and self-service analytics for operators
Partner with BIE on data pipeline requirements — freshness, accuracy, and scalability in Andes/Redshift
Present insights, study results, and methodology recommendations to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
Write quality pillar narratives for quarterly publications and stakeholder newsletters

A day in the life

Monday: Review CBRS cluster refresh — identify sub-cluster movements, flag quality KPI anomalies, prep stakeholder insights. Tuesday: Triage Asana intakes, meet operators to answer benchmark and cluster placement questions.
Mid-week: Strategic alignment with stakeholders on metric logic, long-term vision, and network performance. Meet cross-BU stakeholders on benchmarking expansion needs for quality metrics.
Thursday: Deep methodology work — review site outliers per Quality Pillar KPI, discuss logic changes with regional stakeholders, assess network impact.
Friday: Document weekly quality benchmarking performance, update study progress, share best practices from top stations, field operator gap-closure questions.

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:

Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
Maternity and Parental Leave Options
Paid Time Off (PTO)
401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you!

At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

About The Team

The WW Benchmarking & Standards team establishes the performance truth for Amazon's global last mile network — defining what "good" looks like across 1,000+ delivery stations through statistically validated benchmarks and engineering-grade standards. We set the rates that drive labor planning decisions, publish the WW Scorecard that holds stations accountable to peer-adjusted targets, and run multi-month benchmarking studies that convert underperformance into quantified improvement opportunities.

Our CBRS methodology clusters stations into statistically comparable peer groups, removing excuses and surfacing true operational gaps. We are expanding from retrospective measurement into predictive performance engineering — building risk engines, self-service analytics, and AI-powered tooling that tell operators not just where they stand, but what to do next. The team operates at the intersection of data science, program management, and field operations.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
5+ years of managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership experience

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
Knowledge of general AI tools
Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions
PMP certificate

new_jobs.title: Research Assistant, Public Health-Social Sciences
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Assist with the planning, development, implementation, evaluation, writing and dissemination of the assigned project(s). This position combines research management and academic research skills. This classification requires the use of judgment and discretion in performing the assigned duties and responsibilities related to the project. Position is contingent upon extramural funding.

Impactful Work

Your contributions will directly shape tools that protect scientific rigor and prevent compromised data from influencing research outcomes. You will help researchers work faster, smarter, and with greater confidence in their results.

Creative Problem-Solving

You’ll help create original workflows, AI-enhanced tools, and integrity checks that don’t currently exist. Much of this work involves idea generation, prototyping, testing, and refining.

Professional Growth

You’ll Gain Hands-on Experience With

data validation and integrity methods
automated workflows and reproducibility practices
large-language-model (LLM)–assisted research tools
applied statistics and data quality scoring
the design and delivery of new research-support services

These skills are exceptionally marketable in research, tech, and industry.

Flexibility

A hybrid or remote-friendly arrangement may be possible depending on the candidate and project needs.

Key Responsibilities

Data Quality & Integrity

Run statistical models for data validation, quality checks, and anomaly detection
Identify inconsistent, flawed data using both classical and augmented techniques
Support the development of a data-integrity scoring system for survey and behavioral data
Contribute to best-practice standards, SOPs, and workflows for reproducible science

Augmented Intelligence Workflow & Tool Development

Help design automated workflows that reduce researcher burden (e.g., data processing, QC pipelines, templated processes)
Test and refine generative-AI–informed tools for research support
Build draft templates, protocols, and playbooks for early-career investigators

Research Support & Collaboration

Conduct literature scans and prepare summaries
Assist with drafting manuscripts, reports, and presentations
Collaborate with statisticians, programmers, and faculty to refine and test systems

Service Development & Innovation

Contribute ideas for new research-support products
Help prototype and test new service offerings for faculty (e.g., protocols, automated onboarding workflows, integrated startup kits)
Engage creatively in forecasting what researchers will need 2–3 years from now

Characteristic Work

Work with the PI and senior staff to coordinate the successful and timely completion of tasks that comprise the implementation, data collection and analysis phases of the project to include, but not be limited to planning, development, implementation, evaluation, writing, and dissemination of study findings. Work with project PI or senior personnel to ensure that all aspects of the study are conducted in accordance with the study protocol and grant/contract. Ensure that all study activities comply with state and federal regulations and guidelines, as well as all requirements of the Medical School and University. Train and instruct study personnel about research procedures and protocols. Also, troubleshoot specialized equipment and apparatus as required for the performance of research activities. Participate in site visits when appropriate (e.g., for multi-site studies). Participate in the preparation of progress reports and monitoring quality control. Assist in preparation of posters for study/project(s), and in preparation of posters for national and local scientific meetings. Attend and participate in meetings related to the planning, operation, and evaluation of the study/project, as needed. Perform literature reviews and write summaries. Contribute to the writing of scientific papers for publication from study results. Participate in the writing of new/additional grant proposals. Assist with the budget preparation for new grants and/or projects. Perform other related duties incidental to the work described herein.

Minimum Acceptable Qualifications

Master's degree with at least four years of relevant research experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated knowledge of scientific principles.
Strong computer skills.
Strong communication skills.
Strong foundation in classical statistical methods and quantitative analysis
Experience with data cleaning, data validation, and data management
Demonstrated problem-solving ability and curiosity
Strong writing, communication, and collaboration skills

Additional Desirable Qualifications

Supervisory ability.
Experience beyond the minimum.
Teaching experience.
Public speaking experience.
Prior participation in the preparation of grant proposals.
Peer reviewed publications and/or oral or poster presentations at national meetings.
Interest or familiarity with AI tools, LLMs, or workflow automation
Experience with R, Python, or similar statistical programming tools
Experience contributing to research manuscripts
Ability to work in fast-paced, evolving, “startup” environments
Creative mindset and comfort generating new ideas

Additional Details

Full-time, 1-year position with possibility of renewal
Remote or hybrid options may be considered
Some tasks may require occasional travel or after-hours work depending on project timelines

new_jobs.title: Research Assistant I - Neurology (Dr. Jeevarajan)
new_jobs.description:
This role will support research operations in the Vascular and Interventional Neurology Division, coordinating patient enrollment, data collection, and regulatory compliance for ongoing studies under the supervision of Dr. Jerome Jeevarajan. This position supports ongoing research studies for stroke and other acute injuries, with a major focus on data science and neuroimaging. The team, led by Dr. Jerome Jeevarajan, is involved in multi-center clinical trials and cutting-edge research aimed at developing more precise outcome predictions for patients recovering from severe brain injuries.

Daily tasks will include data entry, brain imaging processing, direct patient interaction, and collaboration with interdisciplinary teams.

Ideal candidates will have experience with clinical research coordination, including clinical data abstraction and obtaining informed consent from patients.

Familiarity with stroke or interventional neurology studies is preferred. Candidates should preferably be proficient in data management software (e.g., iRIS, EPIC, REDCap, Excel), work well in a fastpaced environment, and preferably demonstrate the ability to operate independently with minimal supervision. The ability to communicate effectively with diverse patient populations is preferred.

What we do here changes the world.
UTHealth Houston is Texas’ resource for healthcare education, innovation, scientific discovery, and excellence in patient care. That’s where you come in.

Once you join us you won't want to leave.
It’s because we reward our team for the excellent service they provide. Our total rewards package includes the benefits you’d expect from a top healthcare organization (benefits, insurance, etc.), plus:

100% paid medical premiums for our full-time employees
Generous time off (holidays, preventative leave day, both vacation and sick time – all of which equates to around 37-38 days per year)
The longer you stay, the more vacation you’ll accrue!
Longevity Pay (Monthly payments after two years of service)
Build your future with our awesome retirement/pension plan!

We take care of our employees!
As a world-renowned institution, our employees’ wellbeing is important to us. We offer work/life services such as...

Free financial and legal counseling
Free mental health counseling services
Gym membership discounts and access to wellness programs
Other employee discounts including entertainment, car rentals, cell phones, etc.
Resources for child and elder care
Plus many more!

Position Summary:

The Research Assistant I, under general supervision, conducts basic/ translational research which may include animal work and other activities according to research protocol. Research activities may include some or all of the following: handling biological samples, laboratory experiments and activities, and data collection.

Position Key Accountabilities:

Under general supervision, performs laboratory experiments and activities to support research objectives.
Collects, organize and prepares research data to provide needed information to principal investigators and other researchers. Updates notebooks, records, and databases as needed.

new_jobs.title: Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
We are excited in your interest to join DC Health (The District of Columbia Department of Health), a nationally accredited public health department (https://phaboard.org/) Where our Vision is for Washington, D.C. to be the healthiest city in America. We believe that all people - no matter their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, education level, age, language, religion, ability, or geographic location - should have the opportunity to live healthy lives.

DC Health is focused on providing the essential public health services (10 Essential Public Health Services) necessary to protect and promote the health of all people in all communities and remove systemic and structural barriers that have resulted in health inequities through the Core Competencies for Public Health Professionals (PH Core Competencies.)

Bring your professional career to Washington, D.C., the most dynamic and diverse city in the country. Join us as you are appreciated, developed, and rewarded and play a vital role in DC Health achieving our Strategic Priorities and Values: 

We look forward to reviewing your candidacy, be well and good luck!

Job Summary

This position is located in the Department of Health (DC Health), Community Health Administration (CHA), Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Bureau (HPDP). DC Health promotes health, wellness, and equity across the District, and protects the safety of residents, visitors, and those doing business in the nation’s capital. DC Health believes that all people - no matter their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, education level, age, language, religion, ability, or geographic location - should have the opportunity to live healthy lives. 

The Food Policy Data Analyst will support the Food Policy Council in building a data-driven understanding of the District’s food system. The position will establish indicators, data sources, and tools needed to monitor the food system over time, build and maintain public-facing dashboards that track key metrics across food access, the local food economy, supply chain, and other Food Policy Council priority areas. The position will work closely with District agencies, Food Policy Council members, and community partners to ensure food system data is accurate, accessible and used to inform program and policy decisions.

Duties And Responsibilities

Utilizes databases of information to create program reports, assures integrity of data, and utilizes software programs for retrieval of historical data, requests for information, summary reports and ad hoc analyses. Develops approaches and prepares analytical reports on performance measures, goals, milestones, trends, and improvements. Compiles trend data for required quarterly reporting and participates in management review of reported data and trends. Provides guidance and assists in the implementation of data-sharing with stakeholders, internal and external to DCH. Interprets and applies analytical techniques to procedures to enhance processing, reporting and query capabilities to improve efficiency and accuracy.

Captures, develops, and documents data definitions, rules, data quality requirements, and logical and physical data models based on program requirements. Performs data cleaning and data validation and verification. Determines the most effective approach to data collection and validation, and works independently to obtain needed data. Develops and applies analytical techniques to assist the agency in meeting its grant/research reporting and analysis and value-added intelligence product development objectives. Ensures the quality of deliverables (processes, procedures, reports, data extracts, audit logs) related to requirements, design, implementation, testing, and adherence to reporting standards.

Qualifications And Education

Specialized
Experience:
Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the applicant with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled. To be creditable, one (1) year of specialized experience must be equivalent to at least the next lower grade in the normal line of progression.

Three to five years of experience in data analysis, applied research or GIS including experience working with data sources related to food systems or public health is strongly preferred.

A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, or Public Health is preferred. However a master’s degree in Public Health (with a concentration in biostatistics or epidemiology) is preferred.

Licenses and Certifications

A GIS Professional Certification, Esri technical certification, or data analytics certification is preferred.

Working Conditions / Environment

The incumbent must be able to carry out official duties in a variety of settings and conditions. Routine work will occur primarily in an office setting.

Other Significant Facts

Employment Sponsorship:

Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa currently.

Agency Wide Consideration:

Qualified individuals that submit applications for this vacancy may be considered for other current open vacancies for which they qualify within DC Health.

Tour of Duty:
Monday - Friday  8:15am - 4:45pm

Area of Consideration:
 Open to the Public 

Promotion Potential:

No Known Promotion Potential

Duration of Appointment:
Career Service Term - 13 month appointment

Pay Plan, Series and Grade:
 CS-0301-12

Collective Bargaining Unit (Union):
This position is not in a collective bargaining unit.

Position Designation:

This position has been designated as Security Sensitive

UC Health is an integrated academic health system serving Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. In partnership with the University of Cincinnati, UC Health combines clinical expertise and compassion with research and teaching—a combination that provides patients with options for even the most complex situations. Members of UC Health include UC Medical Center, West Chester Hospital, University of Cincinnati Physicians and UC Health Ambulatory Services (with more than 900 board-certified clinicians and surgeons), Lindner Center of HOPE and several specialized institutes including UC Gardner Neuroscience Institute and the University of Cincinnati Cancer Center.
